median, with the household size of the Stats NZ Low / High A household projection (the

Stats NZ Medium B household projection (living-arrangement propensities change,
modelled on the 2001–2023 censuses) instead of Medium A (propensities held at 2023).
What each row changes compared with the Reference

a starting surplus of 6,812 dwellings (only the excess above the mean + 2 SD) instead of
18,966.

a zero slope imposed at 2048 and household size held constant after it instead of the
2043–2048 secant slope at 2048, continued linearly in 2049–2050.

consents to December 2025 and the projected 2026 population instead of consents to
July 2026 and the observed 2026 population growth.

every factor held at 2025 instead of A1–A3 on the item paths of Horup et al. (2025) and
A4–A5 falling 1% per year.

household size continues linearly from 2023 at the 2018–2023 census-interval pace
instead of the Stats NZ household-size path rebased on 2023.

items made in New Zealand with electricity-intensive production held at 2025 instead of
following their Horup et al. (2025) path.
items mapped to a proxy material held at 2025 instead of following the proxy's path.

new-dwelling size held at its 2016–2025 mean per typology instead of the 2023–2025
mean.

no starting surplus instead of 18,966 vacant dwellings at the start of 2026, absorbed by
2035: (the 2024–2025 building beyond the stock identity, 9,020 dwellings a year, minus
the 1992–2023 census-interval mean, −463) × 2 years; carried because it exceeds the
mean + 2 SD (SD 3,038).
soil carbon loss also on replacement floor area instead of none on rebuilt footprints.

the 2026 overbuild (building above need in 2026–2027 and its continuation, fading at ρ =
0.43) replaces existing dwellings instead of adding to the stock: no surplus, so no
absorption payback and no soil carbon loss on it.

the lowest / highest pooled materials factor when each case study is left out in turn,
instead of the pooled factor (a spread, not a confidence interval).

the materials factor of the lowest / highest single case study of each typology instead of
the pooled typology factor.

the mean of the 1986–2023 censuses on one definition instead of the 2023 census value
(5.39%).

the shape-preserving (PCHIP) end derivative at 2048, continued linearly, instead of the
2043–2048 secant slope at 2048, continued linearly in 2049–2050.

the soil carbon loss of the lowest (Raw) / highest (Organic) soil order on every new
footprint instead of the area-weighted mean over the soil orders of the Auckland land
zoned for urbanisation.
the starting surplus and the 2026 overbuild absorbed by 2030 / 2045 instead of 2035.
note: Reference 25,503 kt. One at a time: not additive, not a joint interval. "No effect": every case within 0.01% of the Reference. Not shown: the superseded-setting rows (completion rate 0.95 and lag 0 months of MODEL v3.3; the never-absorbed overbuild of MODEL v2.1) and the overbuild gap measured against the 2026 requirement (+0.0028%); no census under-construction correction (+0.0000%); maintenance event timing L / n (-0.6961%) (in the data file).
